第 89 章 Using Six-Page Documents to Close Decisions用六页文档关闭决策

Ian Nowland / 伊恩·诺兰

— 第 242 页 —

This chapter describes how you can use a six-page document combined with a one-hour review meeting as a mechanism to close "disagree and commit" style decisions, as I learned managing at Amazon. I have had success with using this for annual team roadmaps and trade-offs of product strategy, delivery plans, and engineering implementations.

本章描述你怎么用六页文档结合一小时评审会议作为机制来关闭「不同意但承诺」风格的决策，正如我在 Amazon 管理时学到的。我成功用这个做年度团队路线图和产品战略、交付计划、工程实现的权衡。

Why Documents?为什么用文档？

For closing a decision, a document is preferred to PowerPoint; here's why:

关闭决策时，文档比 PowerPoint 更受偏好；原因如下：

Clarity. Written documentation forces the writer to clarify their thoughts before discussion and state them in a way that avoids misinterpretation. Introvert inclusion. Documents are more inclusive of introverts who find it difficult to speak during meetings, often because they are thinking deeply about new issues raised. The reader owns rate of information consumption. Written documents can be read at any pace and in any order. They can be pondered. The full argument is seen before conversation. Questions asked are informed by the complete picture rather than where the presenter is in the slides.

清晰。书面文档迫使写作者在讨论前澄清想法，以避免误解的方式陈述。内向者包容。文档对在会议中难以发言的内向者更包容，经常因为他们在深度思考提出的新问题。读者掌握信息消费速度。书面文档可以任何速度和顺序阅读。它们可以被沉思。对话前看到完整论证。问的问题基于完整图景而不是演讲者在幻灯片哪里。

— 第 243 页 —

Conversation rather than dictation. It is easy for PowerPoint to become the presenter giving a speech rather than a conversation among all stakeholders. That being said, documents come with a cost to produce and review. If all stakeholders are happy, a decision can be resolved at a whiteboard, which is preferred. It is as stakeholder groups grow larger, or decisions more contentious, that a document's benefits outweigh its costs.

对话而不是命令。PowerPoint 很容易变成演讲者演讲而不是所有利益相关者之间的对话。话虽如此，文档有生产和评审成本。如果所有利益相关者都高兴，决策可以在白板上解决，那更受偏好。随着利益相关者群体变大、或决策更有争议，文档的好处才超过成本。

Document Structure, Tone, and Format文档结构、语气和格式

The goal of the document is to get disparate stakeholders with different backgrounds to "disagree and commit" consensus on a decision, even when they disagree with it. It does this in three ways. The first is structurally, ensuring just as much space is spent on background as the proposal. Often, it is two pages each on general background, the specific problem, and the proposed decision to solve it. The second is tone, which needs to be "state of the world." This means that it needs to dispassionately state misses rather than be defensive or hide them. Second, disagreements on strategy need to be in the document; they need to be both explicitly stated as disagreements and have their trade-offs discussed. Finally, there's the magic of six (at most) pages of text, which is no more than you'd want to read and discuss closely in one hour. It also means not cheating, having at least 1-inch margins and 10-point font.

文档的目标是让不同背景的不同利益相关者就决策达成「不同意但承诺」共识，即使他们不同意。它通过三种方式做到。第一是结构上，确保背景和提案花同样多的篇幅。通常，一般背景、具体问题和提议的解决方案各两页。第二是语气，需要是「世界状态」。这意味着它需要冷静地陈述失误而不是防御或隐藏。第二，战略上的分歧需要在文档中；它们需要被明确陈述为分歧并讨论权衡。最后，有六页（最多）文本的魔力，不超过你想在一小时内仔细阅读和讨论的量。这也意味着不要作弊，至少 1 英寸边距和 10 号字体。

Getting the Body Down to Six Pages把正文压到六页

The challenge with this format is packing the necessary information into six pages. Here is a guide:

这个格式的挑战是把必要信息塞进六页。以下是指南：

  • Reduce wordiness. For every word ask: what information is it conveying? Eliminate pointless adjectives and subjective and vague terms.减少啰嗦。对每个词问：它在传达什么信息？消除无意义形容词和主观模糊的词。
  • Avoid digressions and pedantic detail. This isn't a thesis assessment.避免离题和迂腐细节。这不是论文评审。
  • Prefer short lists of inarguable points to longer lists that introduce arguable minor points. Arguable minor points take space on paper, head space of the reader, and time in the meeting.偏好短的无可辩驳点列表，而不是引入可争议小要点的长列表。可争议小要点占用纸上空间、读者脑力、会议时间。
  • For background detail that might be important, use appendices. Examples include long tables, detailed graphs. Importantly, there should be no narrative text in appendices.对于可能重要的背景细节，用附录。例子包括长表格、详细图表。重要的是，附录里不应该有叙述文本。
— 第 244 页 —

When you have done this and the body is still more than six pages, it means that there is too much information for a 60-minute review to come to a decision. This is often the case for large proposals when an author covers requirements, design, implementation, and roadmap. Ideally, they instead separate out areas into multiple documents and reviews. If you don't want to spend that time, that is sometimes okay; stakeholders may sometimes be fine deferring agreement on such long documents that required so much work. There is even a saying: the important work is the writing, not the reading. This falls apart, though, when not all stakeholders agree.

当你做了这些正文还超过六页，意味着信息太多，60 分钟评审无法决策。大型提案经常这样，作者覆盖需求、设计、实现和路线图。理想情况下，他们把领域分成多个文档和评审。如果你不想花那个时间，有时候可以；利益相关者可能有时同意推迟对这种需要大量工作的长文档的共识。甚至有句话：重要的工作是写作，不是阅读。然而当不是所有利益相关者都同意时，这就崩了。

Meeting Structure会议结构

Here's the format: 1. Presenter brings hard copies; everyone takes one. 2. First 15 minutes: They sit down and begin reading; no one talks. 3. Next 25 minutes: Presenter "walks the doc," calling out section numbers, asking for comments. 4. Next 15 minutes: Discussion of the decision. 5. Last 5 minutes: Bring the meeting to closure.

格式如下：1. 演示者带纸质副本；每人拿一份。2. 前 15 分钟：他们坐下开始阅读；没人说话。3. 接下来 25 分钟：演示者「走查文档」，报章节号，征求评论。4. 接下来 15 分钟：讨论决策。5. 最后 5 分钟：结束会议。

Reading during the meeting ensures that everyone reads the document as opposed to just glancing over it. That's also why a paper copy is important, so people aren't distracted. Deliberately walking through the document is also important because there is a tendency to jump to discussing the decision. You need to get there, but you want to make sure everyone in the room has had time to ask questions to understand what leads to it. To close the meeting, the document author should be clear as to whether the proposal will go forward and what will happen if not.

会议中阅读确保每个人读文档而不是只是扫一眼。这也是纸质副本重要的原因，这样人们不分心。刻意走查文档也很重要，因为倾向于跳到讨论决策。你需要到达那里，但你想确保房间里每个人有时间问问题理解导致决策的原因。结束会议时，文档作者应该清楚提案是否会推进、如果不推进会怎样。
